title: Observations of the Halo Star HD 177566
comment: 17 pages, 8 figures, to be published in the Astrophysical Journal
summary: We have analyzed archival FUV and optical spectra of the hot halo star HD 177566. The star has an effective temperature $T_{\rm eff} = 33{,}000 \pm 1000$ K, surface gravity $\log g = 3.79 \pm 0.11$, and helium abundance $\log N({\rm He})/N({\rm H}) = -0.86 \pm 0.05$. Abundances of 13 additional elements are consistent with those of other halo stars, save for carbon, which is underabundant by about 1 dex. The low-order hydrogen Balmer lines are not well reproduced by our models. The diffuse lines of He I are often broader than predicted, but the use of more recent line-broadening parameters significantly improves the fit. Scaling our best-fit model to the star's optical and near-IR magnitudes yields an extinction $E(B-V) = 0.095 \pm 0.005$, consistent with literature values, but the resulting model underpredicts the star's FUV flux by a factor of two. The star's effective temperature and luminosity ($\log L / L_{\odot} = 3.50 \pm 0.08$) place it on the post-AGB evolutionary tracks of a star that evolved from the red horizontal branch. Its low carbon abundance, $\log N({\rm C})/N({\rm O}) = -2.18 \pm 0.21$, indicates that it did not experience significant third dredge-up while ascending the AGB.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes FUV and optical spectra of the hot halo star HD 177566, finding it to be a post-AGB star evolved from the red horizontal branch with Teff = 33,000 K, log g = 3.79, and helium abundance log N(He)/N(H) = −0.86. Carbon is underabundant by ~1 dex, and the star's low C/O ratio (−2.18) indicates it did not undergo significant third dredge-up during AGB ascent. The best-fit model underpredicts the FUV flux by a factor of two despite consistent E(B−V) extinction.
AI.motivation: To characterize the physical properties, chemical abundances, and evolutionary status of the hot halo star HD 177566 using archival FUV and optical spectra.
AI.method: Analysis of archival FUV and optical spectra, spectral modeling to determine Teff, log g, and abundances, comparison with post-AGB evolutionary tracks, and scaling model fluxes to photometry for extinction and flux consistency checks.
AI.result: Star has Teff = 33,000 ± 1000 K, log g = 3.79 ± 0.11, helium abundance −0.86 dex, and abundances for 13 other elements consistent with halo stars except carbon (underabundant by ~1 dex). Low-order Balmer lines poorly reproduced; diffuse He I lines improved with newer broadening parameters. Extinction E(B−V) = 0.095 ± 0.005 matches literature, but model underpredicts FUV flux by 2×. Position in HR diagram places it on post-AGB tracks from the red horizontal branch. Log N(C)/N(O) = −2.18 ± 0.21 indicates no significant third dredge-up.
AI.conclusion: HD 177566 is a post-AGB star evolved from the red horizontal branch that did not undergo significant third dredge-up, explaining its low carbon abundance.
